To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the urban environment can be classified into 8 types characterized by different exposures to environmental risk factors, which are measured by HRV and SD.
urban environments differ significantly in their exposure to environmental factors and that noise and social loads are the more significant factors in enhancing human health risks and general SD.

(a) the exposure to urban environmental risk factors varies among different urban environments, and (b) the most significant factors are noise and social load, and (c) these findings can be used to improve urban planning.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach to characterize human exposure to environmental health risks in different types of urban environments and to assess the contribution of different environmental factors to human health risks and general SD.

the development of an urban exposure index (UEI), a new method for assessing exposure to environmental risk in the urban space, and the development of a new approach for the classification of urban environments based on the exposure of human beings to the environment.
the development and application of new methods of environmental health risk assessment based on the concept of urban environmental types.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
urban environments with high noise, CO and social load are more likely to cause discomfort and health risks.
the urban environments that are characterized by high exposure to environmental factors are those with a high level of traffic and a high density of population and buildings.

a set of factors that characterize the urban environment (micro-climate, CO, noise, individual heart rate) and social load can be used to identify the types of urban environments that are associated with higher risk to environmental health.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the urban environment is characterized by different types of urban environment, each one characterized by a unique combination of environmental loads that affect the health of urban dwellers.

a combination of environmental factors, measured in random locations, provides a better understanding of exposure to environmental loads in urban environments than results calculated based only on measurements from close stations.
the results demonstrate significant differences of exposure to environmental risk factor among the different types of urban environments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the urban environments can be classified into 8 types that have different exposure levels to environmental factors and therefore different health risks.
the exposure of the population to environmental health risks varies significantly across the urban environment.
the urban environment is not uniform and the exposure to environmental health risks is not homogeneous.
